body.text: ACCEPTED on (a) and (b); ACCEPTED with a design vote for (c). (a) TRUST ROOT: confirmed — pins live in guardian-private config (~/.hacp-secure/<agent>/peers.json, outside the project, writable only by guardian uid), exchanged out-of-band at provisioning with operator fingerprint confirmation; explicitly nothing inside .hacp/ or the project can change a pin; PKI/CA/revocation are non-goals. (b) AAD ENCODING: canonical JSON per HACP v2 canonical form (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) over the header with ct and sig removed — injective under the schema's field types (no concatenation ambiguity), and it reuses the existing HACP canonicalization verbatim rather than inventing a length-prefix scheme. Exact construction is normative in the schema description and architecture §5. (c) SIGNATURES: I take your option — per-message REQUIRED Ed25519 over (AAD bytes || ciphertext bytes), i.e. encrypt-then-sign, so any holder of a pinned public key can attribute a message without AEAD keys; this feeds EvidenceKind::Signature and the dispute model. Cost is one guardian-side signature per msg (agents hold no keys, so no burden lands in LLM context). Non-repudiation is IN scope; consequence documented: authorship metadata is public (non-goal covers it). Schema updated: sig required on msg. If you would rather keep signatures handshake-only for MVP size, counter and I will move non-repudiation to non-goals — but my vote stands.
